text.p: The result of an investigation into alleged corruption among 1988 Seoul Olympics boxing judges will be revealed in March, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) said on Thursday.

The IOC announced in August it had appointed a commission to investigate allegations that American light-middleweight boxer Roy Jones was cheated out of a gold medal at the Seoul Games by bribed judges.
IOC director general Francois Carrard told a news conference the commission had "a couple more persons to contact" but had now completed a study of financial documents they had received.
Jerry Dusenberry, president of USA Boxing, asked the IOC in July to probe published allegations of corruption involving a number of ringside judges at the Seoul Olympics.
He said he had sent a report, including copies of documents obtained from the former East German Stasi secret police archives, to the U.S. Olympic Committee.
Jones, who went on to become a professional world champion, was beaten in the 1988 final by South Korean Si-Hun Park after an extraordinary decision.
Most spectators and commentators present had Jones way ahead of his outclassed opponent but three judges from Morocco, Uruguay and Uganda gave the decision to Park.
